scope: selected named origins to one named destination, VLCC only

owners.shared_destination_deviation: sum of route-labelled actual-minus-reference deliveries; not another cargo store
owners.routing: one sequential reservation allocator over unique empty ship IDs

units.prompt_ships: integer ships actually open at that origin before dispatch
units.reference_daily_bbl: barrels per operating day in selected VLCC scope
units.movement_ready_turn: integer internal tick; >= departure plus occupied sea/discharge turns
units.tce_real: 2025 USD per standard ship day, indicative benchmark
units.pressure_days: bounded reference-flow-day signal, not physical barrels

rules: A destination empty ship is never prompt at any origin until ballast arrival.
One ship can take at most one departure or repositioning order per turn.
Cargo size belongs to its selected route/class service parcel, not to a global VLCC lot constant.
Actual cargo is discharged exactly once by the completing identified laden movement.
Loaded ships cannot be rerouted; empty movements are also frozen until their ready turn.
No order cancellation, cargo decay, source substitution, or new global demand curve.
Destination pressure is normalized once by the selected routes' total reference daily flow.
Each quote uses half local origin pressure and half shared destination pressure, not multiple copies of total shortage cargo.
Routing forecasts use current and past plan volumes plus bounded physical catch-up; never future Seed volumes.
Reference-cycle target assignment and incoming ballast are diagnostics, not immediately available supply.
Zero ship supply may have an indication but cannot have executed benchmark freight or revenue.
The retained real TCE soft ceiling is a prior experimental guard, not an economic global reservation price.
Non-VLCC quantities and nonselected routes remain outside this fixed submarket fleet.
